question: Ticket 09f5cc38e16f says "evidence['hollow_anchor'][tid]['not_run'] records which teeth this specific host could not run (printed UNRAN) and carries this host-specific information in the seal", but outline 9.4.2.3.3.1 reads "A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks. Seals are made by one sealing machine in the cairn device, and there is only ever one cairn (until a laptop dies and a backup takes over), so there is one sealer. A box that is not cairn's home asks the sealer instead of writing its own seal." (9.4.2.3.3.1 states 'A seal is host independent: one record per proof, whichever box asks.' The ticket makes the seal's contents differ by host—a Windows seal will record different not_run_teeth than a Linux seal for the same proof. This violates the clause 'whichever box asks' should get the same record. The seal is no longer host-independent; different hosts will produce different seal records with different host-specific not_run_teeth arrays.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: Both stand; it is a distinction, not a conflict (CC's adjudication: the hollow anchor is a CC mechanism, and 9.4.2.3.3.1's why decides it). 9.4.2.3.3.1 forbids a second record: one seal per proof, one sealer. not_run is not a second record or a per-box seal. It is a field on that one record saying which declared teeth the reading that made it could not run (they printed UNRAN), so the record does not claim more than was measured (Law 7: a record of truth never collapses an error; CP1). A later reading from the one sealer replaces the field with its own. The record stays one per proof, whichever box asks.
